full_judgment: 6. Admittedly, the suit land measuring 3.37 acres of land (Ga-Schedule including some other lands were recorded in the names of 3 sisters namely, Golejan Bibi, Rupjan Bibi and Sukjan Bibi in equal shares during Cadastral Survey (CS Operation). Exhibit 5 CC Khatian No. 56 stands in support of the contentions as to the previous ownership of the suit land according to the plaintiff's case, Sale Certificate dated 12-1-1954 (Boinama) submitted by the defendant in connection with Rent Execution Case No. 720 of 1953 filed by the ex-landlord Raja Protiva Nath Roy Bahadur against the original plaintiff Karimon Nessa and another CS recorded owner Golejan Bibi (her Khala). It indicates clearly that said plaintiff Karimon Nessa was the owner of the suit land with Golejan Bibi in the year 1953-54 when the auction sale was held. None of the defendant No. 2's predecessors, according to his genealogy given in the written statement, was party to the execution proceedings of the connected Rent suit which he relied on. Had they any interest and possession in the suit land according to the defendant's case, their names ought to have appeared amongst the defaulter tenants against whom auction proceeding was initiated. The defendant No. 2 though set up a separate case stating genealogy of Kichir Mondal, father of the CS recorded tenants as previous owner, he has not been able to establish such contention by substantial evidence in view of consistency in the plaintiffs clear case on the basis of CS Khatian. So, the defendant's case so far his claim of independent ownership through reversion heirs of Kichir Mondal, cannot be acceptable. Further, it is evident that actually the case of the defendant stands on the second contention ie termination of plaintiffs tenancy right, in the suit land on the basis of auction purchase by the ex-landlord Raja Protiva Nath Roy Bahadur. The defendant No. 2 relying on the auction sale submitted Bainanama dated 12-4-1954, which is Exhibit I. After the promulgation of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the suit land, alleged to have been auction purchased by the ex-landlord, vested in the Government as non-retainable Khas land. So, the defendant No. 2 prayed that the suit land was correctly recorded in the name of the Government during SA operation giving a complete go-by to his earlier stand of independent claim of title. Accordingly, the defendant No. 2 took lease from the Government vide Exhibit 3 which shows that the lease was given showing the suit land as khas land of the Government in the year 1974. In such view of the matter, it must be held that the CS Khatian can be taken as the basis of asserting ownership of the suit land and the plaintiff Karimon Nessa was admitted to be owner of the suit land as she was shown as judgment debtor of the Execution Case through which the admitted auction sale took place on 21-11-1953.
